How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?" They provide version:3.1.0, IP:192.168.11.33, API name: get nodes list, Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI.

We need to respond with instructions or code snippet. We can use the tool to call requests_get. Provide the URL with fabricName replaced. Use the function calls. Then we can show how to construct the request. Also mention authentication, headers, etc. Probably they want to know how to generate the request. So we can give example using curl or python requests. Also mention that you need to replace <ip> with actual IP. Provide sample code. Also mention that you might need to set up authentication (username/password or token). Provide steps: open Cisco Nexus Dashboard, navigate to API section, choose GET /nodes, fill parameters, click Generate Request. Or if using script, use python requests library.

Thus answer: explain how to generate request manually: use curl:

curl -k -u username:password "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI"

Also show python:

import requests
url="https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes"
params={"fabricName":"PEK-ACI"}
response=requests.get(url, params=params, auth=('username','password'), verify=False)
print(response.json())

Also mention that you may need to add headers like Content-Type: application/json.

Also mention that you can use the built-in API console in Cisco Nexus Dashboard: go to API Explorer, select GET /nodes, input fabricName, click Execute.
